edges.mechanism: Beta-alanine is a substrate analogue at the taurine transporter (TauT) and competes with taurine uptake. High-dose animal feeding (3-5% in drinking water) depletes plasma/brain/retinal taurine. Human muscle taurine is unchanged at 3.2-6.4 g/d for up to 24 weeks. Whether co-supplementing taurine reduces carnosine loading is untested.
edges.evidence: Cryo-EM structural study; animal depletion studies; human biopsy RCTs and Bayesian MA showing no muscle taurine change; low certainty for any clinical effect

edges.mechanism: Complementary mechanisms: phosphocreatine resynthesis (creatine) and intramuscular H+ buffering via carnosine (beta-alanine). Combination may enhance anaerobic power and repeated bouts, but a network MA found no synergy beyond creatine alone.
edges.evidence: SR of 7 RCTs (n=263) favourable; network MA of 52 RCTs no synergy; small RCT in women no additive benefit; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Intracellular (carnosine) plus extracellular (bicarbonate) buffering. Combination SMD 0.32 (95% CI 0.07-0.57) vs neither alone significant; 2017 MA ES 0.43 (CI 0.22-0.64) for combination vs placebo.
edges.evidence: Two MAs and a systematic review; 2026 RCT in female athletes attributed gains to bicarbonate; moderate-low certainty

edges.mechanism: Common pre-workout co-ingredient. 200 mg caffeine with 3 g beta-alanine acutely raised resting intraocular pressure (caffeine effect; beta-alanine alone did not). No acute additive performance benefit in superset resistance training.
edges.evidence: Two crossover RCTs (n=20-21); relevant mainly to glaucoma; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Carnosine synthesis consumes histidine: beta-alanine 6 g/d lowered plasma (-30.6%) and muscle (-31.6%) histidine; 12 g/d SR lowered plasma histidine. Histidine co-supplementation prevents the fall but does not add carnosine. Pooled human data show no significant muscle histidine change.
edges.evidence: Two RCTs with biopsies; Bayesian MA; low certainty for clinical relevance

edges.mechanism: Taking pure beta-alanine with meals increased soleus carnosine loading (+64% vs +41% between meals), probably through insulin-stimulated uptake.
edges.evidence: Controlled human study (n=34) with 1H-MRS; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Carnosine/beta-alanine supplementation lowered fasting glucose (SMD -0.53) and HbA1c (SMD -0.36) in prediabetes/T2DM, so an additive effect is possible. Most data are from carnosine.
edges.evidence: MA of 8 RCTs (n=377) and Bayesian MA; no direct interaction study; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Dose-dependent, transient tingling via MrgprD-expressing sensory neurons (histamine-independent). OR 8.9 vs placebo. Attenuated by <=1.6 g single doses or sustained-release formulations.
edges.evidence: Risk-assessment MA (101 human studies), kinetic RCT, mechanistic study, ISSN position stand; high certainty for occurrence

edges.mechanism: Animal models show beta-alanine-induced taurine depletion causing cerebellar damage (worse in taurine-deprived cats) and retinal nerve fiber layer thinning. No human equivalent shown.
edges.evidence: Animal studies only; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: No human safety data; reviews note research gaps in pregnancy, nursing and childhood.

Case of severe rhabdomyolysis (CK >120,000 U/L) after prolonged resistance training while using a multi-supplement stack (creatine, beta-alanine, citrulline malate, beta-ecdysterone). Ergogenic stacks may enable larger training loads. Causality is not attributable to beta-alanine.
edges.evidence: Single case report; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Possible improvement in FBG, HbA1c and HOMA-beta with carnosine/beta-alanine; glucose monitoring is reasonable if combined with therapy.
Small true rise in circulating ALT (ES 0.274), with means within reference ranges. 24 weeks at 6.4 g/d showed no change in AST/ALT/ALP/creatinine/CK.
edges.evidence: Bayesian MA and 24-week RCT; moderate certainty

edges.mechanism: Plasma histidine falls with beta-alanine loading (consumed for carnosine synthesis).
Acute oral beta-alanine raised plasma taurine in humans, without increased urinary loss.
